summary: Inheritance makes a new class that starts with all the fields and methods of an existing class. You add new methods or override old ones in the subclass.
notes: class HonorsStudent extends Student names the one parent class, the same keyword as Java.
super(name, scores) must run before the constructor uses this.
super.describe() calls the parent's version of a method you have overridden.
pitfall: Leaving out super(name, scores) causes ReferenceError: Must call super constructor in derived class before accessing 'this' or returning from derived constructor when you create the object.
contrast: JavaScript writes extends and super like Java, but there is no @Override or protected: every field is public unless it uses #, and a # field is not visible to subclasses. Like Python, a missing super() call is caught only when the program runs.
